land.text: El Salvador: 'In 1824, the two jurisdictions were united in the State of Salvador, a part of the Federal Republic of Central America'

predecessors.note: The State of Salvador was one of the five states of the federation ('Costa Rica, El Salvador, Guatemala, Honduras, and Nicaragua'). The federation was dissolved by Carrera's decree of 17 April 1839 (Congress accepted it on 14 July) but El Salvador declared its independence from it only on 30 January 1841; Cliopatria's row begins in 1840.

capitals.name: San Salvador
capitals.note: Infobox capital. San Salvador was the federal capital from June 1834 (Federal Republic page) and the capital of the State of Salvador before and after.

correction.text: the 1840 shape (the present territory of El Salvador) held for 1839 as well: after the decree of 17 April 1839 dissolving the federation the State of Salvador stood alone until it declared independence on 30 January 1841

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria's row begins in 1840 but the federation ended in 1839 (the Federal Republic dossier ends in April 1839 and names El Salvador as a successor); without this year the land would be unowned in 1839.

21,708 km2 against the infobox's 21,041 km2 (ratio 1.03, but the infobox is a present-day figure). The shape is the present territory held unchanged for 139 years; the page gives no border change in the years 1840-1978 (it is silent on the Honduran border, the 1980 treaty and the Gulf of Fonseca islands), so the shape stands.

correction.text: the present territory of El Salvador held through the Salvadoran Civil War (1979-1992): Cliopatria draws nothing for 1979-1991, but the state continued and the Chapultepec accords were signed on 16 January 1992

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria's row has a gap from 1979 to 1991, the years of the civil war; the page shows the government of El Salvador in office throughout ('the government of El Salvador, represented by president Alfredo Cristiani, and the FMLN' signed on 16 January 1992). The page gives no loss of land to the FMLN, so the whole shape is kept.

21,708 km2 against the infobox's 21,041 km2 (ratio 1.03). The page does not mention the 1992 International Court of Justice judgement on the Honduran frontier, so the unchanged shape is not checked against it.
Same shape as 1992; infobox area 21,041 km2 (ratio 1.03).

region.text: El Salvador, the State of Salvador of the Federal Republic of Central America, left on its own by the decree of 17 April 1839

ledger.note: 1839: the federation is dissolved and the State of Salvador stands alone. 'On 17 April, Guatemalan President Rafael Carrera issued a decree dissolving the Federal Republic of Central America; the Federal Congress accepted his decree on 14 July' (the page's infobox gives 17 April 1839). The federation's page does not say what El Salvador did in these months; it declared independence on 30 January 1841, so the birth here is the Cliopatria-compatible one and the declaration is the 1841 event.

1841: the State of Salvador declares itself a sovereign republic. 'El Salvador declared its independence from the Federal Republic of Central America on 30 January 1841'; 'Upon the dissolution of the federation in 1841, El Salvador established full sovereignty as an independent republic' (infobox: international recognition 18 February 1841). The dossier and colour continue; no land changes hands.

wars.name: Football War
wars.outcome: The page names it only as an effect of the expulsion or flight of 'as many as 130,000 Salvadorans' from Honduras; it gives no battles, occupation or treaty, and no change of border.
wars.note: Page silent on the fighting; the dated war page (July 1969) and the 1980 peace treaty with Honduras were not opened (page budget), so no occupation events are recorded. The Honduras group's dossier may carry them.

wars.name: Salvadoran Civil War
wars.outcome: Ended by the Chapultepec Peace Accords, signed on 16 January 1992 by President Alfredo Cristiani and the FMLN; no territory changed hands on the page.
wars.note: Cliopatria has no shape for 1979-1991; the keyframe review adds one.

certainty.note: No page opened gives a boundary survey or treaty line: the Federal Republic page and the El Salvador page are silent on the Guatemalan and Honduran frontiers, the 1980 peace treaty and the 1992 ICJ ruling. A gap-filler should open the El Salvador-Honduras border pages; the frontier is probably sharp after 1992.

sources.title: El Salvador
sources.note: Identity, independence of 30 January 1841, recognition 18 February 1841, infobox area 21,041 km2, capital, civil war and the 16 January 1992 accords, the Football War as a year only.

sources.title: Federal Republic of Central America
sources.note: The five states, the 17 April 1839 decree and 14 July acceptance, San Salvador as federal capital, the 30 January 1841 declaration.

notes: Start 1839/4 is a choice: the El Salvador page dates its birth to the declaration of 30 January 1841 (a 'rename' event records it), but Cliopatria's shape starts 1840 and the Federal Republic dossier ends in April 1839, so 1839 would otherwise be blank. Move the start to 1841 only if the federation's dossier is extended. Cliopatria gap 1979-1991 is filled by a new keyframe (civil war years). Not settled with two pages: the Honduran frontier (the 1969 Football War occupation, the 1980 General Treaty of Peace, the 1992 ICJ judgement on the land and islands in the Gulf of Fonseca), the Guatemalan frontier; the Cliopatria shape is one constant outline (21,708 km2) for every year, so any border change after 1840 is missing. Counterparts honduras and guatemala exist as dossiers of group am-08. Gazetteer: no new names.
